facts.fact: Burkina Faso's regulator ARCEP hosted the 4th Working Groups Meeting of WATRA, the West Africa Telecommunications Regulators Assembly (16 member states), in Ouagadougou, concluding on 2026-04-12 (the article of 13 April says 'yesterday'), where the groups finalised reports on 5G, cable resilience, cybersecurity, consumer protection and NGSO satellites.

facts.fact: On 2025-11-21 in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso's ARCEP signed an agreement with Ghana's regulator on free roaming between Burkina Faso and Ghana (local tariffs for travellers), in the presence of the digital ministers' delegations; the minister said it will be extended progressively to Mali and Niger.

On 2025-11-21 in Ouagadougou, ARCEP signed with its Ghana, Mali and Niger counterparts a protocol on border frequency coordination (preferential frequencies, interference prevention, 15 km coordination zones each side of borders).

facts.fact: leFaso.net, relaying a Burkina Faso ministry release, reports that digital ministers and experts of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, members of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), met in Ouagadougou on 3-5 November 2026 to finalise digital cooperation documents.

Sidwaya reports Burkina Faso led a three-day workshop of 64 experts from the AES states that finalised the digital deliverables of the Confederation's Year II roadmap in Ouagadougou on 5 November 2026.
In September 2026 the telecom and postal regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed in Ouagadougou a convention creating the Council of Sahel Regulators.
Startup Medias reports the AES digital roadmap, 16 of 18 deliverables finalised, was adopted in Ouagadougou on 5 November 2026 by delegations of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.
Agence Ecofin reports Burkina Faso signed bilateral roaming agreements with Benin, Cote d'Ivoire and Senegal in Ouagadougou on 23 October, with entry into force expected in about three months.
Agence Ecofin reports Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger concluded a roaming agreement under the AES Confederation in November 2024, its operation announced for January 2025 with no recent confirmation.
Niger's regulator director general says AES free roaming among Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger was already operational before the regulators' convention was signed on 25 September 2026.
ARCEP Burkina Faso and Ghana's NCA signed a free roaming MoU on 21 November 2025 in Ouagadougou, the NCA says; launch is planned for April 2026.

ARCEP Burkina and Ghana's NCA finalised and signed a border frequency coordination agreement, and Burkina Faso signed the AES border frequency coordination framework drafted at Niamey in October 2025, ARCEP says.
Regulators of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso signed a memorandum of understanding on free roaming among Alliance of Sahel States members in Niamey, reported by Le Sahel (ONEP).
